identity.title: Torsional-rotational spectrum of doubly deuterated dimethyl ether (CH<SUB>3</SUB>OCHD<SUB>2</SUB>). First ALMA detection in the interstellar medium

paper_type_evidence.quote: For the astronomical detection, we used the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) observations from the Protostellar Interferometric Line Survey, PILS.
The PILS program is an unbiased molecular line survey of the protostellar system IRAS 16293-2422 with ALMA (project id: 2013.1.00278.S; PI: Jes Jørgensen).

targets.name: IRAS 16293-2422 B (position offset 0.5 arcsec to the southwest)

question.value: Measure and fit the 0.15-1.5 THz ground-state rotational spectrum of both conformers of doubly-deuterated dimethyl ether (CH3OCHD2), then use the predictions to detect it toward IRAS 16293-2422 B in ALMA PILS data

evidence.quote: This paper presents the first analysis of the 2D-DME from 0.15 to 1.5 THz (or 150 to 1500 GHz) and reports its detection toward the B component toward IRAS 16293-2422.
(project id: 2013.1.00278.S; PI: Jes Jørgensen)

method.value: Absorption spectroscopy 150-1500 GHz with the Lille spectrometer, 2f demodulation preferred, InSb bolometer detector

evidence.quote: The absorption spectra were measured between 150 and 1500 GHz using the Lille spectrometer (cite: zakharenko2015).
Absorption signals were detected by an InSb liquid He-cooled bolometer (QMC Instruments Ltd.).

key_parameters.value: Typical pressures 35-60 Pa at room temperature; 220 cm long, 6 cm diameter cell

evidence.quote: The measurements were performed at typical pressures of 35-60 Pa at room temperature.

key_parameters.value: Line frequency uncertainties 30, 50 and 100 kHz depending on S/N and frequency range

evidence.quote: Estimated uncertainties for measured line frequencies are 30 kHz, 50 kHz, and 100 kHz depending on the observed S/N ratio and the frequency range.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit effective Hamiltonian to the laboratory lines

method.value: Weighted least-squares fit with the ERHAM code (combined axes method) for each conformer; 15 pure rotational and 5 torsion-rotation parameters; congested high-Ka bQ series removed and only isolated lines kept

evidence.quote: To treat the internal rotation, we used the ERHAM code (cite: groner1997; groner2012).
For each conformer, a set of 15 pure rotational and 5 torsional-rotation parameters of the effective Hamiltonian implemented in the ERHAM code was needed to fit the observed molecular lines.
we decided to remove these congested lines from the final fit and to include only the lines from such series that could be considered as isolated ones.

key_parameters.value: ISCD = -1 and alpha = 0 for the symmetric conformer; ISCD = +1 and alpha fixed to 0 for the asymmetric conformer

evidence.quote: Therefore, in the ERHAM code, the symmetry parameters ISCD is set to $-1$ and $\alpha$, the angle between the rho vector and $ab$ principal axes plane, is set to $0$.
Consequently, for the asymmetric conformation, ISCD=$+1$ and after various attempts to set a value to $\alpha$, we have decided to fix the parameter to 0

assumptions.value: The two conformers are treated as two independent asymmetric tops each with one methyl internal rotor; tunneling between configurations ignored

evidence.quote: In this study, the two conformations of 2D-DME were considered as two independent asymmetric top molecules each with a single unsubstituted CH$_3$ internal rotor.

fitting.value: Weights equal to the reciprocal of the squared measurement accuracy

evidence.quote: In the weighted least-squares fit implemented in the ERHAM code, the weight of each frequency is calculated as reciprocal of the measurement accuracy squared.

validation.value: Weighted rms deviations close to 1 and absence of extra splittings support the independent treatment

evidence.quote: the weighted rms deviations of the fits close to 1 support our initial strategy to treat the two conformations independently

analysis_steps.goal: Estimate the internal rotation barrier V3

method.value: BARRIER program combining the A-E ground-state splitting with the internal rotation constant F

evidence.quote: we used the program BARRIER which is derived from the program ASTOR described in (cite: groner1986) that determines the potential barrier for a single simple internal rotor from torsional transitions or splittings.

assumptions.value: Relative error of V3 taken equal to the relative errors of the A-E energy difference and of the tunneling coefficient epsilon_10

evidence.quote: The estimated error of the $V_3$ barriers is derived with the assumption that the relative error of $V_3$ is the same as the relative errors of the $\Delta  E(E-A)$ energy difference and the tunneling coefficient $\varepsilon_{10}$.

validation.value: Barrier heights compared with the mono-deuterated and parent dimethyl ether studies

evidence.quote: The determined barrier heights agree well with the results of the study of monodeuterated DME (cite: richard2013)

analysis_steps.goal: Compute line predictions and partition functions

method.value: ERHAM V16g-R3 predictions in JPL catalog format up to 1.5 THz; partition functions at 9 temperatures from ERHAM output, compared with a rigid-rotor approximation

evidence.quote: using the ERHAM software in its “ERHAM V16g-R3” version (downloaded on the PROSPE website (cite: kisiel2001)), we calculated predictions in the JPL catalog format (cite: pickett1991) up to 1.5 THz
Numerical values of overall partition functions were computed at 9 different temperatures using the ERHAM output

key_parameters.value: Degeneracy factor g_n = 1 for symmetric and 2 for asymmetric conformer in the rigid-rotor approximation

evidence.quote: the degeneracy factor $g_n$ is equal to 1 for the symmetric conformation and 2 for the asymmetric one

validation.value: Rigid-rotor partition function agrees with the fit-based values to a ratio of 1.002-1.058; only the fit-based values were used for column densities

evidence.quote: However, only the results from the fit, highlighted in bold, were used to derive column densities.

evidence.quote: We then perform $\chi^2$-fitting to the reasonably isolated lines to constrain the column densities of the symmetic and asymmetric conformers separately.

fitting.value: Chi-squared fit of column density with all other parameters fixed; priors and uncertainties not stated

evidence.quote: The factor 2.3 we derive when fitting the two conformers independently is consequently an additional verification of the assignment of the two conformers.
